BURSEVI:v9p237/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r1.claim: The two upper bodies and two lower plant forms supply food—grains, fruit, and fodder; the unlinked opening clauses imitate enumeration and rebuke failure to give thanks, while the star clause is joined because upper and lower pairs contrast and all obey God.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r1.anchor: وكلاهما من قبيل النبات الذي هو أصل الرزق من الحبوب والثمار والحشيش للدواب وإخلاء الجمل الأولى عن العطف

BURSEVI:v9p237/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r2.claim: The nominal syntax for these four forms, unlike the human addressee, marks their difference in essence and attributes.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r2.anchor: ولما كانت هذه الأربعة مغايرة لجنس الإنسان في ذاته وصفاته غير النظم بإيرادها في صورة الاسمية

BURSEVI:v9p237/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r3.claim: Inwardly, the star is the intellect that guides toward knowledge but fades before divine realities unless it receives divine unveiling; the tree is thought, confined to natural, imaginative, and bodily powers and unable to grasp realities fully.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى سجود نجم العقل الذي به يهتدي إلى معرفة الأشياء واستهلاكه وتلاشيه عند النظر إلى الحقائق الإلهية

BURSEVI:v9p237/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p237/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p237/r4.claim: Reason and thought circle the created cosmos but melt when they look to the Creator; being created and bounded, they cannot comprehend the eternal God, whom people have not measured as He deserves.
BURSEVI:v9p237/r4.anchor: العقل والفكر جالا حول سرادق الكون فإذا نظرا إلى المكون ذابا وكيف لا وهما مخلوقان محصوران

QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r4.claim: One lexical distinction calls plants without a trunk stars and those with a trunk trees; another says celestial stars and rooted trees prostrate as signs of the Creator’s majesty.
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r4.anchor: النجم من الأشجار : ما ليس له ساق ، والشجر : ما له ساق

MAJAZ:v2p242/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p242/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p242/r2.claim: الشجر is vegetation with a trunk; النجم grows from the earth without a trunk, and the verb is dual to match the two nouns.
MAJAZ:v2p242/r2.anchor: «والنجم والشجر يسجدان» (6) الشجر ما كان على ساق

NAHHAS:v4p303/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p303/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ibn Abi Talha, takes النجم to mean plants spread on the ground, such as greens, and الشجر to mean a rooted tree.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r5.anchor: روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال النجم ما تبسط على الأرض من الزرع يعني البقل

NAHHAS:v4p303/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p303/r6.claim: Nahhas prefers the broad sense that everything submits to God.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r6.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وهذا أحسن ما قيل في معناه أي يسجد له كل شيء أي ينقاد لله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r6.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي وسفيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r6.claim: They take النجم as stemless ground vegetation, named for sprouting or appearing and fittingly paired with trees.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس والسدي وسفيان: النجم. النبات الذي لا ساق له،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r7.claim: They take النجم as the class of stars, parallel to earthly trees because each appears in its own realm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة والحسن: النجم اسم الجنس من نجوم السماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r8.claim: The word شجر relates to the intertwining of tree branches.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r8.anchor: وسمي الشجر من اشتجار غصونه وهو تداخلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r9.claim: Mujahid says the star prostrates by setting, while vegetation prostrates through its shadow and turning; this applies to either star interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r9.anchor: فقال مجاهد: ذلك في النجم بالغروب ونحوه، وفي الشجر بالظل واستدارته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r10.claim: Mujahid also treats prostration figuratively as submission and humility; a poetic line depicts hills prostrating to hooves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا ما معناه: أن السجود في هذا كله تجوز، وهو عبارة عن الخضوع والتذلل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r11.claim: The dual verb يسجدان agrees with the singular collective-form wording for the kinds, as illustrated by collective nouns with dual verbs in poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224/r11.anchor: وقال: يسجدان وهما جمعان، لأنه راعى اللفظ، إذ هو مفرد اسم للنوع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r1.claim: After agreeing that trees are rooted plants, Ibn Abbas defines al-najm as low-growing vegetation; Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and al-Thawri agree, and Ibn Jarir prefers this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r1.anchor: النجم ما انبسط على وجه الأرض -يعني من النبات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r2.claim: They identify al-najm as a star; Ibn Kathir prefers this because another verse lists stars with other beings bowing to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#3/r2.anchor: النجم الذي في السماء. وكذا قال الحسن وقتادة. وهذا القول هو الأظهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r18.claim: He identifies the star as the stars of heaven collectively.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r18.anchor: نجم السماء , وهو موحد والمراد به جميع النجوم , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r19.claim: Alternatively, the star is a low-growing plant without a stem, contrasted with trees that have trunks.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r19.anchor: النجم النبات الذي قد نجم في الأرض وانبسط فيها , ليس له ساق , والشجر ما كان على ساق , قاله ابن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r20.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r20.claim: Their prostration is the prostration of their shadows.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r21.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r21.claim: Their form and power display the workmanship that requires submission.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r21.anchor: ما فيهما من الصنعة والقدرة التي توجب السجود والخضوع

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r22.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r22.claim: Their prostration is the movement of their shadows, as in the verse about shadows turning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r22.anchor: دوران الظل معهما ، كما قال تعالى : { يتفيأ ظلاله } ، قاله الزجاج

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r23.claim: Alternatively, the star prostrates by setting and the tree by allowing its fruit to be picked.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r23.anchor: سجود النجم أفوله ، وسجود الشجر إمكان الإجتناء لثمارها

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r24.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r24.claim: The star and tree face the rising sun, then incline with it as the shadow shifts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r24.anchor: أنهما يستقبلان الشمس إذا أشرقت ثم يميلان معها إذا انكسر الفيء

MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.claim: Low plants without stems and trees with stems prostrate through their shadows as the sun moves; the sky is raised 500 years above earth, and the balance establishes justice, requiring people not to cheat in measures.
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.anchor: { والنجم } يعني كل نبت ليس له ساق { والشجر } كل نبت له ساق

TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r4.claim: A common interpretation calls najm vegetation without a trunk and shajar plants with trunks; the author regards this as good and supported by their pairing.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r4.anchor: قالوا المراد بالنجم ما ينجم من النبات ويطلع من الأرض ولا ساق له، والشجر ما له ساق من النبات، وهو

TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r5.claim: Their prostration is obedience to God's command to grow, or more precisely the roots' penetration of soil to draw nourishment expresses their dependence on God as prostration.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r5.anchor: وأدق منه أنهما يضربان في التراب بأصولهما وأعراقهما لجذب ما

TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the connection of these clauses to the Merciful is semantic: the calculation is His and the prostration is to Him.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r6.anchor: قال في الكشاف فإن قلت كيف اتصلت هاتان الجملتان بالرحمن يعني قوله

TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains that the first clauses enumerate separate blessings to rebuke deniers, then coordination resumes for related clauses.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#2/r7.anchor: عن العاطف ما محصله أن هذه الجمل الأول واردة على سنن التعديد

TABRISI:55:1-13/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r5.claim: Ḥusbān is a verbal noun of reckoning or a plural of ḥisāb; najm is low vegetation without a stem, shajar is stalked vegetation, and ālāʾ are blessings with singular forms cited from Abū ʿUbayda.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r5.anchor: والحسبان مصدر حسبته أحسبه حسابا وحسبانا

TABRISI:55:6-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، سفيان الثوري
TABRISI:55:6-10/r2.claim: The star is earth's low vegetation without a stem; the tree has a stem and survives winter.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r2.anchor: يعني بالنجم نبت الأرض الذي ليس له ساق وبالشجر ما كان له ساق

TABRISI:55:6-10/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r3.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
TABRISI:55:6-10/r3.claim: Alternatively, najm means the heavenly stars collectively, which prostrate to God morning and evening along with trees.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r3.anchor: وقيل: أراد بالنجم نجم السماء وهو موحد والمراد به جميع النجوم

TABRISI:55:6-10/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:6-10/r4.claim: Prostration may mean that these things are signs of their origination and of their maker's artistry and power, calling for submission.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r4.anchor: إن المعنى في سجودهما هو ما فيهما من الآية الدالة على حدوثهما

TABRISI:55:6-10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r5.speaker: الضحاك، سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:55:6-10/r5.claim: Another view identifies their prostration with their shadows; the shadows also demonstrate origination and a directing Creator.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r5.anchor: سجودهما سجود ظلالهما كقوله يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل

TABRISI:55:6-10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r6.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:55:6-10/r6.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains prostration as submission because God directs these things without resistance; prostration can mean humility.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r6.anchor: معنى سجودهما أنه سبحانه يصرفهما على ما يريده من غير امتناع

THALABI:v9p177#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#3/r1.claim: Ḥusbān may be a verbal noun, like ghufrān and kufrān, or a plural of ḥisāb, like other broken plurals.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r1.anchor: والحسبان قد يكون مصدر حسبت حسابا وحسبانا مثل الغفران والكفران والرجحان والنقصان

THALABI:v9p177#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#3/r2.claim: The sun and moon's raised syntactic position may be explained by an elided verb, or they may be a subject whose predicate follows.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r2.anchor: وارتفاع الشمس والقمر بإضمار فعل مجازه الشمس والقمر يجريان بحسبان

THALABI:v9p177#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#3/r3.claim: One arrangement connects the statement to the preceding mention of the Merciful teaching the Quran and measuring the sun and moon; another links it back to the explanation.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r3.anchor: ونظم الآية الرحمن علم القرآن وقدر الشمس والقمر

THALABI:v9p177#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p177#3/r4.claim: A transmitted account describes words written on the faces and interiors of the sun and moon, proclaiming God's unity, creation, power, and the moral consequences of good and evil.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r4.anchor: مكتوب في وجه الشمس: لا إله إلا الله، محمد رسول الله، خلق الشمس بقدرته،

THALABI:v9p177#3/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v9p177#3/r5.claim: One interpretation says najm is low-growing plants without a trunk that spread over the ground; their prostration is their shadow.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r5.anchor: قيل: هو ما ليس له ساق من الأشجار، وينبسط على وجه الأرض

THALABI:v9p177#3/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r6.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v9p177#3/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says najm collectively refers to plants, named for rising from the earth; their prostration is their shadow.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: هو جمع النبات سمي نجما لطلوعه من الأرض، وسجودها سجود ظلها

THALABI:v9p177#3/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p177#3/r7.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
THALABI:v9p177#3/r7.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify najm as a celestial star, whose prostration is its rising.
THALABI:v9p177#3/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: هو الكوكب، وسجوده طلوعه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:6-13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:6-13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:6-13/r1.claim: “The star/herb” is vegetation without a stalk that does not survive winter; plants and trees prostrate by submitting to God’s will.

ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r2.claim: Najm is a ground-growing plant without a stem, while shajar is a stemmed plant; both prostrate by obeying God's will and adapting to His natural laws, so people should willingly obey and prostrate in gratitude.
ELMALILI:55:1-13#2/r2.anchor: necim yani Arz’dan zuhur edip de sâkı olmayan nebat, çimen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r6.claim: Here najm means stemless plants such as grain and grass, although the word can also mean stars; the plant sense is generally accepted.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r6.anchor: necm kelimesi, tahıl ve ot gibi gövdesi olmayan bitkileri ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r7.claim: The prostration of trees and plants means their involuntary submission to God's laws; human beings can consciously revere God and obey, which gives their choice special dignity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r7.anchor: Ağaçların ve diğer bitkilerin secde etmesi, bunların Allah’ın yasalarına iradî olmaksızın boyun eğmelerini ifade etmekte

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r2.claim: Rather than demand a new sign, opponents should reflect on the familiar signs of the heavens, earth, and the worlds within and around them, which teach the Qur’an’s lesson.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r2.anchor: why do not they deliberate on the signs of the heavens and the earth and the world found inside man and that outside him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r4.claim: The discourse points to signs within and around people, repeatedly warning humans and jinn to reflect and asking how many signs they will deny.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r4.anchor: the various signs in the world around man and those within him are pointed to and two of the Almighty’s creations – men and jinn– are repeatedly warned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r4.claim: The regular, punctual paths of the sun and moon are signs that teach people to obey their Creator’s laws.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r4.anchor: the sun and the moon adhere to their paths with such punctuality and discipline. There is never a discrepancy even of a second.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r5.claim: The sun and moon remain within their distinct ordained paths and never intrude on one another’s course.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r5.anchor: Never does the sun exceed its ordained path to intrude into the path ordained for the moon nor does the moon intrude into the path ordained for the sun

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r6.claim: The sun and moon’s obedience to limits is called taqwā in religious terminology and teaches humans to abide by God’s laws.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r6.anchor: After mentioning how the sun and the moon abide by the limits ordained for them and which in religious parlance is called taqwā

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r7.claim: If people break the laws God has established throughout the universe and spread anarchy, they will be punished.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r7.anchor: If man breaks these laws and dares spread anarchy in this world, why would He not punish him?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r8.claim: Stars and trees prostrate before their Creator, calling people to submit and worship in obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p112/r8.anchor: the stars of the heavens and trees of the earth: they bow down before their Creator and through this practice of theirs call upon man

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r1.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r1.claim: Some interpreters take najm to mean small plants, thorny trees, or creepers; Islahi regards this as far-fetched.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r1.anchor: Probably, they were not able to understand the purpose of mentioning trees with stars and for this reason they had to make this far-fetched interpretation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r2.speaker: Mujāhid, Qatādah and Ḥasan
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r2.claim: Mujāhid, Qatādah, and Ḥasan take najm in its conventional sense of stars; Ibn Kathīr supports this interpretation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r3.claim: Stars and trees share attributes and are rightly mentioned together, showing harmony between heaven and earth under one Creator; both prostrate to Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p113/r3.anchor: there exists great commonality in the attributes of the two.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r9.claim: The star and tree pair earthly traces and human sustenance with the sun and moon; the stemless food plant comes first as staple, while tree fruit is often a treat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r9.anchor: ولما ذكر تعالى ما أنعم به من منفعة الشمس والقمر، وكان ذلك من الآيات العلوية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r10.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r10.claim: They take النجم as heavenly stars; the apparent reading is the stemless plant paired with الشجر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن النجم هو الذي شرحناه، ويدل عليه اقترانه بالشجر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r11.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r11.claim: The star prostrates by setting and the tree through its shadow; Mujahid also reads prostration figuratively as submission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r11.anchor: وسجودهما، قال مجاهد والحسن: ذلك في النجم بالغروب ونحوه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r12.claim: The later clauses rely on semantic rather than pronoun linkage; both prostrate to God, and the ordering pairs celestial with earthly things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p55/r12.anchor: والجمل الأول فيها ضمير يربطها بالمبتدأ، وأما في هاتين الجملتين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r6.claim: Najm means a plant without a stem; a tree has a stem that lasts through winter. Their prostration is their shadows, as in the Qur'an's description of shadows bowing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r6.anchor: النجم ما ليس له ساق من النبات، والشجر ما له ساق يبقى في الشتاء، وسجودهما سجود ظلهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r7.claim: Mujahid says najm means a star and its prostration is its rising.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442/r7.anchor: قال مجاهد: النجم هو الكوكب وسجوده طلوعه.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r1.claim: The stars include celestial bodies and low-growing plants, while trees are rooted plants; both ‘prostrate’ by submitting to their appointed courses and yielding their benefits.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r1.anchor: أي وجميع الكواكب السماوية وكل نبت ارتفع من الأرض ولا ساق له

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r2.claim: The submission of sun, moon, stars, and trees points to the Creator’s unity and chosen action, refuting natural forces as independent causes.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r2.anchor: مما يدل على وحدانية الصانع وفعله بالاختيار , ونفي الطبائع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p50#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p50#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p50#2/r1.claim: Al-najm is a plant without a stem, from a verb meaning to appear or emerge; al-anam means living creatures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p50#2/r1.anchor: النجم: النبات الذي لا ساق له، من نجم: أي ظهر وطلع. الأنام: الحيوان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r4.claim: The star is the lower powers and the tree the higher predispositions; both humble themselves before God when returning to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r4.anchor: القوى السفلية ( والشجر ) الأستعدادات العلوية ( يسجدان ) يتذللان بين يديه تعالى عند الرجوع إليه سبحانه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r7.claim: Al-najm here means stemless plants that emerge from the earth, such as vegetables, while al-shajar means trees with trunks.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r7.anchor: والنبات الذي ينجم من الأرض لا ساق له كالبقول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r8.claim: The plants' prostration is their submission to God in the purpose for which He created them and their inability to resist, likened to a worshipper's obedient prostration.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r8.anchor: تشبيها بالساجد من المكلفين في انقياده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r9.claim: The clauses about calculation and prostration connect by meaning without a verbal conjunction: the calculation belongs to God and the prostration is to Him alone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r9.anchor: استغنى فيهما عن الوصل اللفظي بالوصل المعنوي ، لما علم أن الحسبان حسبانه ، والسجود له لا لغيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.claim: The first clauses omit conjunctions so each independently rebukes deniers by enumerating benefactions; conjunctions resume for clauses that suit and approach each other.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.anchor: ثم رد الكلام إلى منهاجه بعد التبكيت في وصل ما يجب وصله للتناسب والتقارب بالعاطف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r11.claim: The two clauses suit one another because sun and moon are celestial, plants earthly, heaven and earth are paired, and celestial calculation resembles the plants' submission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r11.anchor: إن الشمس والقمر سماويان ، والنجم والشجر أرضيان ، فبين القبيلين تناسب من حيث التقابل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r15.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r15.claim: Mujāhid takes al-najm to mean the stars of the sky, rather than stemless vegetation.

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.claim: The sun and moon among celestial signs are paired with the stars and trees prostrating among earthly signs.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r3.anchor: وقال : { الشمس والقمر } ( القيامة : 9 ) في العلويات وقال في مقابلتهما من السفليات : { والنجم والشجر يسجدان } ( الرحمن : 6 )

STUDYQURAN:55:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r1.claim: The verse depicts all celestial and earthly entities prostrating in submission to God, as in 22:18 and 16:49.
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r1.anchor: this verse alludes to the prostration before God of all celestial and earthly entities

STUDYQURAN:55:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r2.claim: Although najm is singular, it is understood collectively to mean all stars.
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r2.anchor: Stars translates najm, which occurs in the singular, but is understood as a reference to all stars.

STUDYQURAN:55:6/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r3.speaker: Aj, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r3.claim: Najm may instead mean herbs or all soft-stemmed plants, contrasted with trees as hard-stemmed plants.

STUDYQURAN:55:6/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r4.claim: Whether najm means stars or herbs, their prostration signifies complete submission to God's Will.
STUDYQURAN:55:6/r4.anchor: In either interpretation, their prostration is an indication of their complete submission to God’s Will.

TAB-FULL:v22p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r1.speaker: أبو رزين وسعيد
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r1.claim: Abu Razin and Said say the prostration of the star and tree is their shadows prostrating.
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r1.anchor: عن زبرقان، عن أبي رزين، وسعيد

TAB-FULL:v22p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r2.claim: Qatada says every created thing sent down from heaven worships God, willingly or unwillingly.

TAB-FULL:v22p177/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r3.claim: Mujahid says the star and tree prostrate in the morning and evening.
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {والنجم والشجر يسجدان} [الرحمن: 6]

TAB-FULL:v22p177/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r4.speaker: الفراء
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r4.claim: Al-Farra says Arabic commonly uses a singular verb with paired nonhuman collective nouns, as in sheep and cattle or palms and lote trees; using a dual verb is also permissible.
TAB-FULL:v22p177/r4.anchor: وقد زعم الفراء أن العرب إذا جمعت الجمعين من غير الناس مثل السدر والنخل، جعلوا فعلهما واحدا

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r7.claim: Al-najm means a plant that sprouts from the earth without a trunk, such as grapevine or pumpkin.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r7.anchor: أي النبات الذي ينجم أي يطلع من الأرض ولا ساق له مثل الكرم والقرع

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r8.speaker: المنتقى
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r8.claim: Al-Muntaqa distinguishes a plant that stops growing within its year from a tree, which continues to grow rather than being cut off in its year.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r8.anchor: وفي المنتقى كل نابت إذا ترك حتى يبرز انقطع فليس بشجر وكل شيء يبرز ولا ينقطع من سنته فهو شجر

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r9.claim: Their prostration means their natural submission to God's will, analogous to the voluntary prostration of morally responsible worshippers.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r9.anchor: أي ينقادان له تعالى فيما يريد بهما طبعا انقياد الساجد من المكلفين طوعا

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, the plants' shadows prostrate, as described in the verse about shadows turning to the right and left.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r10.anchor: أو يسجد ظلهما على ما بين في قوله تعالى يتفيأ صلاله عن اليمين والشمائل

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r11.claim: The text also invokes the Quranic reminder that people do not comprehend the creatures' glorification of God.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r11.anchor: كما قال تعالى : "ولكن لا تفقهون تسبيحهم"

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r12.claim: The two earthly blessings, plants and trees, are set opposite the two heavenly blessings, the sun and moon.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r12.anchor: ذكر في مقابلة النعمتين السماويتين اللتين هما الشمس والقمر نعمتين أرضيتين وهما النجم والشجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135/r1.speaker: عامة أهل اللغة والمفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135/r1.claim: Most linguists and exegetes define najm as ground vegetation without a trunk, and shajar as trunked vegetation that lasts through winter, unlike najm.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135/r1.anchor: قال عامة أهل اللغة والمفسرين: النجم: النبت على الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r1.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says najma is a small plant, plural najm; najama can mean to emerge or sprout, as a horn, star, or tooth rising.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: النجمة نبتة صغيرة وجمعها نجم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن الحارث بن ظالم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda cites al-Ḥārith b. Ẓālim’s line as evidence for najm meaning a plant the donkey tries to uproot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r2.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة للحارث بن ظالم (¬2): أخصيي حمار ظل يكدم نجمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r3.claim: Al-Azharī explains that the donkey’s effort to pull out the plant strains its body, accounting for the poem’s wording.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r3.anchor: قال الأزهري: وإنما قال ذلك لأن الحمار إذا أراد أن يقلع النجمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r4.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r4.claim: Al-Layth cites a verse describing a garment woven from abundant najm, as poetic evidence for the plant sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r4.anchor: وأنشد الليث: موزر بعميم النجم تنسجه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r5.claim: Exegetes take najm as what the earth has sprouted; al-Wāḥidī has not found linguists using anjama to mean “to grow.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r5.anchor: ذكر المفسرون في تفسير النجم: هو ما أنجمت الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r6.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī say Arabic often gives two nonhuman plurals one singular verb, though dual agreement is possible; dual agreement here matches the line endings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r6.anchor: قال الفراء والكسائي: العرب إذا جمعت جمعين من غير الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r7.claim: Exegetes explain the plants’ prostration as the prostration of their shadows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r7.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير في معنى سجود النجم والشجر أنه سجود أظلالهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r8.claim: The author links the prostration of shadows to 16:48.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r8.anchor: وقد ذكرنا ذلك في قوله: {يتفيأ ظلاله عن اليمين والشمائل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid identifies najm as the stars of heaven and says the trees prostrate morning and evening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {والنجم} قال نجوم السماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r10.claim: Qatāda also identifies najm here as the stars.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r11.claim: Abū Isḥāq allows the literal prostration of the stars, since God says that stars prostrate to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p135#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬4): وهذا جائز أن يكون الله أعلمنا أن النجم يسجد

QASHANI:55:3-6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:3-6/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:3-6/r4.claim: The star is the sentient animal soul in the body's night, and the tree is its nourishing vegetative soul; both prostrate by turning wholly toward the body's earth to nurture and perfect it.
QASHANI:55:3-6/r4.anchor: أي: النفس الحيوانية النورانية بالشعور الحسي في ليل الجسم

BURHAN:v3p444/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p444/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p444/r1.claim: Tawriya uses a shared word with a near and distant sense, intending the distant one while leading the hearer toward the near; here al-najm means low-growing plants, though the hearer may think of a star, especially after sun and moon.
BURHAN:v3p444/r1.anchor: وهي أن يتكلم المتكلم بلفظ مشترك بين معنيين قريب وبعيد

BURHAN:v3p376/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r1.claim: In the preceding example, the past tense is stronger in meaning than a passive participle, but the weaker form is chosen to make the paired wording parallel.
BURHAN:v3p376/r1.anchor: فإن قلت الماضي أدل على المقصود من أسم المفعول فلم عدل عنه إلى ما دلالته أضعف

BURHAN:v3p376/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r2.claim: A present participle can replace a future form to match the wording: in 51:6, the participle denotes the present, not inherently the future.
BURHAN:v3p376/r2.anchor: ومنه العدول عن المستقبل إلى اسم الفاعل

BURHAN:v3p376/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r3.claim: One kind of verbal matching makes the second expression resemble the first; examples include a neighboring-word reading in ablution and the transition from the trees' prostration to the heaven's raising.
BURHAN:v3p376/r3.anchor: أحدهما وهو الأكثر المشاكلة بالثاني للأول نحو أخذه ما قدم

BURHAN:v3p376/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r4.claim: Verbal matching can also make the first expression resemble the second; Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿUbayla's kasra reading of al-ḥamdu lillāh is cited as more eloquent.
BURHAN:v3p376/r4.anchor: وقد تقع المشاكلة بالأول للثاني كما في قراءة إبراهيم بن أبي عبيلة الحمد لله بكسر الدال

BURHAN:v3p376/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p376/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p376/r5.claim: Wording can match the meaning's character: a weighty expression suits a weighty meaning, while a lowly one suits a diminishing comparison.
BURHAN:v3p376/r5.anchor: ومتى كان اللفظ جزلا كان المعنى كذلك

ITQAN:v2p332#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p332#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p332#2/r1.claim: Al-najm refers to plants that spread along the ground, while al-shajar grows on a stem.
ITQAN:v2p332#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ والنجم والشجر ﴾ النجم ما ينبسط على الأرض والشجر ما ينبت على ساق

ITQAN:v3p227/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p227/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p227/r2.claim: The word najm can mean a star, suggested by the mention of sun and moon, or the more remote intended sense of stemless plants; this is a Qur'anic double entendre.
ITQAN:v3p227/r2.anchor: فإن النجم يطلق على الكوكب ويرشحه له ذكر

ITQAN:v3p247/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p247/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p247/r1.claim: This is an instance of combining multiple things under one judgment: the sun and moon follow a reckoning, while the star or plant and tree prostrate.

DAMGHANI:v1p229/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r13.claim: Sujūd can mean submission and surrender; the stars and trees submit to God.
DAMGHANI:v1p229/r13.anchor: الثالث : السجود الانقياد والاستسلام قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

DAMGHANI:v1p258/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p258/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p258/r9.claim: Shajar here means every tree that has a trunk.
DAMGHANI:v1p258/r9.anchor: الشجرة كل شجرة لها ساق قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

DAMGHANI:v1p449/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p449/r1.speaker: غريب القرآن
DAMGHANI:v1p449/r1.claim: Al-najm means plants: what sprouts from the earth without a trunk; the cited source contrasts this with trees that have trunks.
DAMGHANI:v1p449/r1.anchor: النجم ما نجم من الأرض أي طلع ولم يكن على ساق كالعشب والبقل والشجر ما قام على ساق قال في غريب القرآن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r2.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r2.claim: Najm can mean a plant without a stalk, distinguished from a stalk-bearing tree in the verse about both prostrating.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p580/r2.anchor: والثاني : النبت الذي لا ساق له

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r1.claim: In ordinary Arabic, prostration is lowering the head even without touching the ground; every submissive person is called prostrating.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r1.anchor: السجود في اللغة : خفض الرأس وإن لم تصل الجبهة إلى الأرض . وكل ذليل فهو ساجد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r4.claim: Sujūd can mean compliance and submission.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p348/r4.anchor: والثالث : الانقياد والاستسلام . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r1.claim: Shajar is the plural of shajara and denotes any plant with a trunk.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r1.anchor: الشجر : جمع شجرة . وهي كل نبات له ساق

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r2.claim: Shajir, a valley, or land can describe a place abundant in trees.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r2.anchor: وواد شجير : كثير الشجر . وهذه الأرض أشجر من هذه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r3.claim: The verb shajara can describe a dispute among people.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r3.anchor: وشجر بين القوم : إذا اختلف الأمر بينهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p379/r4.claim: Shajar can mean a tree with a trunk.

FARRA:v3p112/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112/r2.claim: النجم means plants that sprout, such as grass and herbage; الشجر means what grows on a trunk.
FARRA:v3p112/r2.anchor: النجم: ما نجم مثل: العشب، والبقل وشبهه. والشجر: ما قام على ساق

FARRA:v3p112/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112/r3.claim: Their prostration is that they face the rising sun and lean with it until the shadow begins to recede.
FARRA:v3p112/r3.anchor: وسجودهما: أنهما يستقبلان الشمس إذا طلعت، ثم يميلان معها حتى ينكسر الفيء

FARRA:v3p112/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112/r4.claim: Arabic often treats two nonhuman collectives with a singular verb, as with sheep and livestock or palms and lote trees, though dual agreement is valid.
FARRA:v3p112/r4.anchor: والعرب إذا جمعت الجمعين من غير الناس مثل: السدر، والنخل جعلوا فعلهما واحدا

FARRA:v3p112/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112/r5.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v3p112/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi heard سودان and سود for two black sheep; al-Farrāʾ prefers سود as the better dual adjective.
FARRA:v3p112/r5.anchor: قال الكسائي: سمعت العرب تقول: مرت بنا غنمان سودان وسود.

FARRA:v3p112/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112/r6.claim: With masculine sheep and feminine camels, singular feminine agreement is most common; masculine or feminine dual agreement is also correct.
FARRA:v3p112/r6.anchor: فإذا كان أحد الاثنين مؤنثا مثل: الشاء والإبل قالوا: الشاء والإبل مقبلة

FARRA:v3p112/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112/r7.claim: In قومك وإبلهم قد أقبلوا, the verb can refer to the people who move the camels or to both groups, since mixed humans and animals take human agreement.
FARRA:v3p112/r7.anchor: لأن الناس إذا خالطهم شيء من البهائم، صار فعلهم كفعل الناس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r1.claim: Al-najm here means grass and herbage.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r2.claim: Al-shajar means plants that stand on a stem.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says their prostration is that they face the sun at sunrise, then lean with it as the shade declines.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r3.anchor: قال الفراء (2) : "سجودهما: أنهما يستقبلان الشمس إذا أشرقت ثم يميلان معها حتى ينكسر الفيء".

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains prostration as the submission of inanimate things and their compliance with what they are made subject to.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#4/r4.anchor: وقد بينت السجود في كتاب "تأويل المشكل" (3) وأنه الاستسلام من جميع الموات (4) ، والانقياد لما سخر له.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p237/r1.claim: The stars and trees prostrate by submitting to God through subjugation.

ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة وأكثر أهل التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r3.claim: Linguists and most exegetes define al-najm as any plant without a trunk, and al-shajar as anything with a trunk.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r3.anchor: قال أهل اللغة وأكثر أهل التفسير: النجم كل ما نبت على وجه الأرض مما ليس له ساق

ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r4.claim: The prostration of plants and trees is the turning of their shade with them, as described in 16:48.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى سجودهما دوران الظل معهما كما قال: (أولم يروا إلى ما خلق الله من شيء يتفيأ ظلاله

ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r5.claim: Another possible referent for al-najm is the stars.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r5.anchor: وقد قيل إن النجم أيضا يراد به النجوم

ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r6.claim: The star interpretation is possible because God says that those in the heavens and earth, including the sun, moon, and stars, prostrate to Him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r6.anchor: قد أعلمنا أن النجم يسجد، فقال: (ألم تر أن الله يسجد له من في السماوات ومن في الأرض

ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r7.claim: The word may cover both earthly growth and the stars, since anything that appears or rises is called najama.
ZAJJAJ:v5p95#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون النجم ههنا يعني به ما نبت على وجه الأرض وما طلع من نجوم السماء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī uses “najm” for vegetation without a stem and “tree” for vegetation with a stem.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ والنجم والشجر يسجدان ﴾ قال النجم كل شيء ليس له ساق

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says the intended meaning here is the star.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p262#2/r2.anchor: قال معمر قال قتادة إنما يريد النجم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r1.claim: The sentence about the plants prostrating is a predicate coordinated with the preceding predicate.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، أبو رزين
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Abu Razin take النجم as low-growing plants that emerge from the earth without a stem, and الشجر as plants with stems.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r2.anchor: والمراد بالنجم النبات الذي ينجم أي يظهر ويطلع من الأرض ولا ساق له وبالشجر النبات الذي له ساق وهو المروي عن ابن عباس وابن جبير وأبي رزين

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r3.claim: Their prostration is their submission to God’s will as it governs their natural behavior.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r3.anchor: والمراد بسجودهما انقيادهما له تعالى فيما يريد بهما طبعا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r4.claim: This is an explicit derivative metaphor: natural behavior is likened to a prostrator’s submission and reverence for its creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r4.anchor: شبه جريهما على مقتضى طبيعتهما بانقياد الساجد لخالقه وتعظيمه لهثم استعمل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r5.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة، الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r5.claim: Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Hasan take النجم to mean the stars of the sky, whose prostration is their setting or the like.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة والحسن النجم نجم السماء وسجوده الغروب ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r6.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r6.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan explain the trees’ prostration through their shadows and their turning.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r6.anchor: وسجود الشجر بالظل واستداره عند مجاهد والحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r7.claim: In another report, Mujahid explains both prostrations as submission to whatever God naturally wills for them.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r7.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عن مجاهدأن سجودهما عبارة عن انقيادهما

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r8.claim: The majority’s botanical interpretation is preferable because النجم is paired with الشجر, though the preceding mention of sun and moon suggests the familiar celestial meaning and creates an evident double meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r8.anchor: والجمهور على تفسير النجم بما سمعت أولاقبل لأن اقترانه بالشجر يدل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r9.claim: Earlier clauses omit conjunctions to enumerate separate blessings and stir gratitude; adding conjunctions might make them seem like one blessing, despite their close relation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r9.anchor: وإخلاء الجمل الثانية والثالثة والرابعة عن العطف لورودها على نهج التعديد مع الإشارة إلى أن كلامما تضمنتهمستقلة تقتضي الشكر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r10.claim: The conjunction between the fourth and fifth clauses pairs heavenly sun and moon with earthly plants and trees, both obedient to God’s command.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r10.anchor: وتوسيط العاطف بين الرابعة والخامسة رعاية لتناسبهما من حيث التقابل لما أن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r11.claim: There is no verbal connective between the clauses because their semantic relation is unmistakable: the celestial bodies follow God’s reckoning and the plants prostrate to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r11.anchor: وخلوهما عن الرابط اللفظي مع كونهما خبرين للتعويل على كمال قوة الارتباط المعنوي

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the missing conjunctions as a way to enumerate and emphasize blessings one by one, prompting reflection and rebuking deniers; the ordered list resumes after that rhetorical stirring.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r12.anchor: وفي الكشف : تبيينالما ذكره صاحب الكشاف

ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r13.claim: The clause الشمس والقمر بحسبان is not a predicate of the implicit subject; al-Zamakhshari was explaining its semantic connection to the enumeration.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p100/r13.anchor: وجملة ( الشمس والقمر بحسبان ) ليست من أخبار المبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p101/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101/r1.claim: The author says the interpretation has gone too far, although the apparent wording of al-Zamakhshari’s discussion suggests that الشمس والقمر بحسبان is one of the predicates; he leaves the issue for reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p101/r1.anchor: وقد أبعدالمغزي فيما أرى إلآ أن ظاهر كلام الكشاف يقتضي كون قوله تعالى : ( الشمس

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r2.claim: Al-najm is a plant emerging from earth without a stem; al-shajar is a plant with a stem.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r2.anchor: والنبات الذي ينجم أي يطلع من الأرض ولا ساق له

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r3.claim: The plants submit to God's will by nature, like accountable worshippers who prostrate willingly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r3.anchor: ينقادان لله تعالى فيما يريد بهما طبعا انقياد الساجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r4.claim: The expected parallel wording would say sun and moon run and plants are made to prostrate, or state explicitly that they prostrate to God; the ellipsis is obvious.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r4.anchor: وكان حق النظم في الجملتين أن يقال: وجرى الشمس والقمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r5.claim: The omitted connective is clear enough not to need stating; the conjunction links the two groups as evidence that changes in celestial and terrestrial bodies follow God's decree and governance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r5.anchor: إشعارا بأن وضوحه يغنيه عن البيان

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r6.claim: The conjunction links the celestial and terrestrial phenomena, showing their changes are governed by God's decree.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:5-6/r6.anchor: وإدخال العاطف بينهما لاشتراكهما في الدلالة

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the “najm” is vegetation spread over the ground, while “shajar” is what grows on a trunk.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3322#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : والنجم والشجر يسجدان قال : النجم ما انبسط على الأرض ، والشجر ما كان على ساق .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r2.claim: The clause about stars and trees is coordinated with the sun and moon as a transition from heavenly favors to earthly ones; al-najm can refer to stars or ground plants and bridges the pair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r2.anchor: عطف على جملة { الشمس والقمر بحسبان } ( الرحمن : 5 ) عطف الخبر على الخبر للوجه الذي تقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r3.claim: The coordinated clause leaves the refrain's list-of-favors style: it aims to awaken reflection on a symbolic sign of divine power, and its two terms make a contrasting pair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r3.anchor: فالإخبار بسجود النجم والشجر أريد به الإيقاظ إلى ما في هذا من الدلالة على عظيم القدرة دلالة رمزية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r4.claim: The clause begins with its subject like the clause it follows, and the imperfect verb conveys prostration that continually recurs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r4.anchor: وأتي بالمسند فعلا مضارعا للدلالة على تجدد هذا السجود وتكرره على معنى قوله تعالى :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r5.claim: Al-najm can be a collective noun for the stars or a singular noun whose plural is nujum; the Quran uses both forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r5.anchor: اسم جمع على نجوم السماء قال تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r6.claim: Mujahid identifies al-najm here as the stars of heaven.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r6.anchor: وعن مجاهد تفسيره هنا بنجوم السماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies al-najm here as low-growing plants without a stem.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس تفسير النجم في هذه الآية بالنبات الذي لا ساق له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r8.claim: Al-najm can mean grass or vegetation without a stalk, close to the soil; al-shajar is rooted vegetation with an elevated stem, and both benefit people and animals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p235/r8.anchor: ويطلق النجم على النبات والحشيش الذي لا سوق له فهو متصل بالتراب . وعن ابن عباس تفسير النجم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r1.claim: The pairs of sun and moon, then stars and trees, yield balanced correspondences in motion and stillness, a complete rhetorical embellishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r1.anchor: فحصل من قوله : { والنجم والشجر يسجدان } بعد قوله : { الشمس والقمر بحسبان } ( الرحمن : 5 ) قرينتان متوازيتان في الحركة والسكون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r2.claim: Sujud can mean placing the face on the ground in reverence or, by metaphor or metonymy, falling toward the ground; a laden palm is called prostrate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r2.anchor: والسجود : يطلق على وضع الوجه على الأرض بقصد التعظيم ، ويطلق على الوقوع على الأرض مجازا مرسلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r3.claim: Stars prostrate by descending toward their settings, low plants by clinging to soil, and trees by bending in wind and lowering branches within reach of fruit pickers and leaf gatherers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r3.anchor: فسجود نجوم السماء نزولها إلى جهات غروبها ، وسجود نجم الأرض التصاقه بالتراب كالساجد ، وسجود الشجر تطأطؤه بهبوب الرياح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r4.claim: The verb also figures their downward approach to people and their shadows on Earth as prostration, revealing God's greatness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r4.anchor: فعل { يسجدان } مستعمل في معنيين مجازيين وهما الدنو للمتناول والدلالة على عظمة الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r5.claim: Imru al-Qays's image of leaning on chins evokes a person falling face-first, using an implied metaphor of prostration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r5.anchor: فقال : على الأذقان ، ليكون الانكباب مشبها بسقوط الإنسان على الأرض بوجهه ففيه استعارة مكنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r6.claim: Created things offer rational signs that God made and subjected them; some or most also carry symbolic and imaginative signs accessible to minds with different capacities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p236/r6.anchor: ففي جميعها دلالات عقلية ، وفي بعضها أو معظمها دلالات أخرى رمزية وخيالية لتفيد منها العقول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل واللغويون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r1.claim: One view takes al-najm as every plant without a stem; Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, Muqātil, and the linguists hold it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنه كل نبت ليس له ساق وهو مذهب ابن عباس والسدي ومقاتل واللغويين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r2.claim: Mujāhid instead identifies al-najm as the stars of the sky collectively.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r2.anchor: والثاني أنه نجم السماء والمراد به جميع النجوم قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r3.claim: Al-shajar means all plants that have a stem.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r3.anchor: فأما الشجر فكل ما له ساق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains their prostration as their facing the sun at sunrise and leaning with it until the shadow declines.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r4.anchor: قال الفراء سجودهما أنهما يستقبلان الشمس إذ أشرقت ثم يميلان معها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r5.claim: For how beings without reason prostrate, the commentary directs the reader to its discussion at 16:49.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r5.anchor: وقد أشرت في النحل 49 إلى معنى سجود ما لا يعقل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the verb is dual because the two subjects are dual in wording.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة وإنما ثني فعلهما على لفظهما

MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says al-najm here means the stars of the sky.
MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال أما ﴿ النجم ﴾ فيعني نجوم السماء

MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says trees prostrate in the morning and evening.
MUJAHID:v2p639#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال أما ﴿ النجم ﴾ فيعني نجوم السماء و ﴿ الشجر ﴾ الشجر يسجدان بكرة وعشيا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r1.claim: Al-najm is a low-growing plant without a stem, such as herbs; al-shajar is a tree with a trunk. Another view takes al-najm to mean the stars or heaven.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ والنجم ﴾ النبات الذى ينجم من الأرض لا ساق له كالبقول

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r2.claim: The plants and trees prostrate by submitting to Allah in the functions for which they were created, like the obedience of prostrating worshippers.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r2.anchor: من المكلفين في انقياده واتصلت هاتان الجملتان بالرحمن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r3.claim: The clauses join semantically: the sun and moon follow His reckoning and the plants and trees prostrate to Him. Earlier favors were listed without conjunction to rebuke deniers; the conjunction resumes the pattern and pairs celestial bodies with earthly ones, and their measured courses with submission.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#2/r3.anchor: واتصلت هاتان الجملتان بالرحمن بالوصل المعنوى لما علم ان الحسبان حسبانه والسجود له لا لغيره كانه قيل الشمس والقمر بحسبانه والنجم والشجر يسجدان له

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and others say najm is a plant without a trunk, while shajar has a trunk.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: النجم ما لا ساق له والشجر ما له ساق

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r8.speaker: صفوان بن أسد التميمي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas cites Safwan ibn Asad's verse, where anjama describes low plants emerging on a plain.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r8.anchor: وأنشد ابن عباس قول صفوان بن أسد التميمي: لقد أنجم القاع الكبير

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r9.speaker: زهير بن أبي سلمى
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r9.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses najm for plants woven by the south wind around water.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r9.anchor: وقال زهير بن أبي سلمى: مكلل بأصول النجم تنسجه ريح الجنوب

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r10.claim: Najm derives from something appearing or rising.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r10.anchor: واشتقاق النجم من نجم الشيء ينجم بالضم نجوما ظهر وطلع

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r11.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says their prostration is the prostration of their shadows.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r12.claim: Al-Farra says they face the rising sun and incline with it until their shadows shorten.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r12.anchor: وقال الفراء: سجودهما أنهما يستقبلان الشمس إذا طلعت

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj says their prostration is the movement of their shadows, as in the verse about shadows folding back.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r13.anchor: وقال الزجاج: سجودهما دوران الظل معهما، كما قال تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r14.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r14.claim: Hasan and Mujahid identify najm as a star; Mujahid says its prostration is its moving shadow, the view al-Tabari chooses.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r14.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: النجم نجم السماء، وسجوده في قول مجاهد دوران ظله

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r15.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r15.claim: Al-Mawardi reports a star prostrates by setting and a tree by making fruit available to pick.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r15.anchor: وقيل: سجود النجم أفوله، وسجود الشجر إمكان الاجتناء

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r16.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r16.claim: Al-Qushayri says all are subject to God, so stars and trees must not be worshiped; prostration is submission and a sign of createdness.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r16.anchor: وقيل: إن جميع ذلك مسخر لله، فلا تعبدوا النجم

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r17.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r17.claim: Al-Nahhas says sujud fundamentally means submission and obedience to God, including inanimate things and animals, as well as prayer prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r17.anchor: النحاس: أصل السجود في اللغة الاستسلام والانقياد لله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r18.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r18.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid cites a poem using najm to mean stars.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:5-6/r18.anchor: وأنشد محمد بن يزيد في النجم بمعنى النجوم قال:
